title: Homily III — Greeting her at the tomb, and the closing prayer

edition.locus: Migne, PG 96 (Paris, 1860), Homily III on the Dormition, col. 761 (PDF leaf 422)

source_text:
Δεῦτε, πάντες νοερῶς ἐκδημούσης συνεκδημήσωμεν. Δεῦτε, πάντες καρδίας πόθῳ πρὸς τὸν τάφον κατιούσῃ συγκαταβῶμεν. Περιστοιχήσωμεν τὸν ἱερώτατον κράββατον. Ὕμνους ἱεροὺς ᾄσωμεν, ὧδέ πως μελῳδοῦντες· Χαῖρε, κεχαριτωμένη, ὁ Κύριος μετὰ σοῦ. Χαίροις, ἡ προωρισμένη Μήτηρ Θεοῦ. Χαίροις, ἡ προεκλελεγμένη τῇ πρὸ αἰώνων βουλῇ τοῦ Θεοῦ, γῆς θειότατον βλάστημα, πυρὸς θείου κατοικητήριον, Πνεύματος ἁγίου ἱερώτατον ἄγαλμα, ὕδατος ζῶντος πηγή, παράδεισος τοῦ τῆς ζωῆς ξύλου, θείου βότρυος κλῆμα ἔμψυχον νέκταρ καὶ ἀμβροσίαν πηγάζοντος, ποταμὸς πλήρης τῶν ἀρωμάτων τοῦ Πνεύματος, ἄρουρα τοῦ θείου ἀστάχυος, ῥόδον τῇ παρθενίᾳ φανώτατον, καὶ πνέων τῇ εὐωδίᾳ τῆς χάριτος, κρίνον τοῦ βασιλικοῦ ἀμφιάσματος, ἀμνὰς ἡ τεκοῦσα τὸν Ἀμνὸν τοῦ Θεοῦ, τὸν αἴροντα τὴν ἁμαρτίαν τοῦ κόσμου, τῆς σωτηρίας ἡμῶν ἐργαστήριον, ἀγγελικῶν ὑπερτέρα δυνάμεων, δούλη καὶ μήτηρ.

Δεῦτε, τὸν τάφον περιστοιχήσωμεν τὸν ἀκήρατον, καὶ θείας ἀρυσώμεθα χάριτος. Δεῦτε, ψυχικαῖς ἀγκάλαις τὸ ἀειπάρθενον σῶμα βαστάσωμεν, καὶ συνεισέλθωμεν ἔνδον τοῦ μνήματος, καὶ συννεκρωθῶμεν, τοῖς μὲν τοῦ σώματος ἀπογινόμενοι πάθεσι, συζῶντες δὲ ζωὴν ἀπαθῆ καὶ ἀκήρατον· ἀκουτισθῶμεν τοὺς θείους ὕμνους ἐξ ἀΰλων τῶν ἀγγελικῶν χειλέων προϊεμένους. Εἰσέλθωμεν προσκυνήσοντες, καὶ γνῶμεν τοῦ μυστηρίου τὸ ξένον, ὡς ἦρται, ὡς μεμετεώρισται, ὡς πρὸς οὐρανὸν εἴληπται, ὡς τῷ Υἱῷ πασῶν ὕπερθεν τῶν ἀγγελικῶν παρίσταται τάξεων· οὐδὲν γὰρ μέσον Μητρὸς καὶ Υἱοῦ.

Τοῦτόν σοι τὸν ἐξόδιον λόγον τρίτον ἐπὶ τοῖς δυσὶ πεποίημαι, Μῆτερ Θεοῦ, αἰδοῖ καὶ πόθῳ τῆς Τριάδος ᾗ ἐλειτούργησας τῇ πατρικῇ εὐδοκίᾳ, καὶ τῇ δυνάμει τοῦ Πνεύματος, τὸν ἄναρχον Λόγον, τὴν παντοδύναμον τοῦ Θεοῦ δεξαμένη σοφίαν καὶ δύναμιν. Δέχου τοίνυν τὴν προθυμίαν, τὴν δύναμιν ὑπεραίρουσαν, καὶ δίδου τὴν σωτηρίαν, παθῶν ψυχικῶν ἀλλοτρίωσιν, νόσων σωματικῶν λώφωσιν, περιστάσεων λύσιν, βίου γαληναίαν κατάστασιν, φωτισμὸν Πνεύματος· τὸν πρὸς τὸν σὸν Υἱὸν πόθον ἐκπύρσευσον, εὐάρεστον αὐτῷ τὸν βίον ἡμῶν κατάστησον, ὡς ἂν καὶ τῆς ἐκεῖθεν τυχόντες μακαριότητος, τῇ Υἱοῦ δόξῃ ὁρῶντές σε ἐξαστράπτουσαν, ὕμνους ἱεροὺς ἀναπέμψωμεν, αἰωνίως εὐφραινόμενοι, ἐν ἐκκλησίᾳ ἑορταζόντων ἀξίως τοῦ Πνεύματος, τῷ διά σου τὴν σωτηρίαν ἡμῶν οἰκοδομήσαντι, Χριστῷ τῷ Υἱῷ τοῦ Θεοῦ καὶ Θεῷ ἡμῶν· ᾧ ἡ δόξα καὶ τὸ κράτος, σὺν τῷ ἀνάρχῳ Πατρί, καὶ τῷ παναγίῳ καὶ ζωοποιῷ Πνεύματι, νῦν, καὶ ἀεί, καὶ εἰς τοὺς σύμπαντας καὶ ἀτελευτήτους αἰῶνας τῶν αἰώνων. Ἀμήν.
pass_a_gloss: [0] Come (δεῦτε), all, intellectually/in mind (νοερῶς) with her departing abroad let us depart with. Come, all, with longing (πόθος) of heart to her going down (κατιούσῃ) to the tomb let us go down with. Let us stand around the most sacred bier (κράββατος). Holy hymns (ὕμνοι) let us sing, chanting somehow thus: Hail/rejoice (χαῖρε), one favoured with grace, the Lord with you. Hail (χαίροις), the foreordained Mother of God. Hail, the one chosen beforehand by the before-ages counsel (βουλή) of God, most divine (θειότατον) shoot (βλάστημα) of earth, dwelling of divine fire, most sacred ornament/delight/image (ἄγαλμα) of the Holy Spirit, spring (πηγή) of living water (ὕδωρ ζῶν), paradise of the tree (ξύλον) of life, a living (ἔμψυχον) branch (κλῆμα) of the divine cluster (βότρυς) gushing nectar (νέκταρ) and ambrosia (ἀμβροσία), river (ποταμός) full of the spices/fragrances (ἀρώματα) of the Spirit, field (ἄρουρα) of the divine ear of grain (ἄσταχυς), rose (ῥόδον) most bright (φανότατον) in virginity and breathing with the fragrance (εὐωδία) of grace, lily (κρίνον) of the royal robe (ἀμφίασμα), ewe-lamb (ἀμνάς) the one having borne (τεκοῦσα) the Lamb (Ἀμνός) of God, the one taking away (αἴροντα) the sin (ἁμαρτία) of the world, workshop of our salvation (σωτηρία), higher (ὑπερτέρα) than angelic powers (δυνάμεις), slave/servant (δούλη) and mother. [1] Come, let us stand around the undefiled (ἀκήρατος) tomb, and let us draw (ἀρυσώμεθα) divine grace. Come, with soul-arms the ever-virgin body let us carry, and let us enter with within the tomb (μνῆμα), and let us die with, on the one hand to the passions (πάθη) of the body being dead/ceasing, on the other living with (συζῶντες) a passionless (ἀπαθής) and undefiled life; let us be made to hear the divine hymns from immaterial (ἄϋλα) angelic lips (χείλη) being sent forth. Let us enter to venerate, and let us know (γνῶμεν) the strangeness (τὸ ξένον) of the mystery (μυστήριον): how she has been lifted (ἦρται), how she has been raised aloft, how to heaven she has been taken (εἴληπται), how to the Son above all the angelic ranks (τάξεις) she stands by (παρίσταται); for nothing (is) between (μέσον) Mother and Son. [2] This exodus/departure (ἐξόδιος) discourse (λόγος), third after the two, I have made for you, Mother of God, in reverence (αἰδώς) and longing for the Trinity (Τριάς), to which you ministered by the paternal good pleasure (εὐδοκία) and the power (δύναμις) of the Spirit, having received the unoriginate (ἄναρχος) Word, the all-powerful wisdom (σοφία) and power of God. Receive (δέχου) then the eagerness (προθυμία), the (one) exceeding the ability (δύναμις), and give (δίδου) salvation, estrangement from soul-passions, abatement (λώφησις) of bodily diseases (νόσοι), release (λύσις) from difficulties, a calm (γαληναία) state of life (βίος), illumination (φωτισμός) of the Spirit; the longing toward your Son kindle, well-pleasing (εὐάρεστον) to him establish (κατάστησον) our life, so that also having attained (τυχόντες) the blessedness (μακαριότης) from there (ἐκεῖθεν), seeing you flashing out with the Son's glory (δόξα), we may send up holy hymns, eternally rejoicing, in an assembly (ἐκκλησία) of those keeping festival worthily of the Spirit, to the one having built through you our salvation, Christ the Son of God and our God; to whom the glory and the might (κράτος), with the unoriginate Father, and the all-holy and life-making (ζωοποιόν) Spirit, now, and always, and to the whole and endless ages of the ages. Amen.
pass_b_english: Come, let us all go out in spirit with her as she departs. Come, let us all, with the longing of our hearts, go down with her as she goes down to the tomb. Let us stand around the most holy bier. Let us sing holy hymns, chanting something like this: “Rejoice, you who are full of grace; the Lord is with you (Luke 1:28). Rejoice, you who were foreordained to be Mother of God. Rejoice, you who were chosen beforehand in the counsel of God before the ages: most divine shoot of the earth, dwelling-place of divine fire, most holy ornament of the Holy Spirit, spring of living water, paradise of the tree of life, living branch of the divine cluster of grapes that pours out nectar and ambrosia, river full of the fragrances of the Spirit, field of the divine ear of grain, rose most radiant in virginity and breathing out the fragrance of grace, lily of the royal robe, ewe who bore the Lamb of God, who takes away the sin of the world (John 1:29), workshop of our salvation, higher than the angelic powers, servant and mother.”

Come, let us stand around the undefiled tomb and draw divine grace. Come, let us carry the ever-virgin body in the arms of our souls, and go in with her into the tomb, and die with her, dying to the passions of the body, but living with her a life free of passion and undefiled. Let us listen to the divine hymns that come from the immaterial lips of the angels. Let us go in to venerate, and come to know the strangeness of the mystery: how she has been lifted up, how she has been raised on high, how she has been taken up to heaven, how she stands beside her Son above all the ranks of angels. For nothing stands between Mother and Son.

This third discourse on your departure, after the two before it, I have made for you, Mother of God, in reverence and love for the Trinity, whom you served when, by the good pleasure of the Father and the power of the Spirit, you received the Word who has no beginning, the all-powerful wisdom and power of God (1 Corinthians 1:24). Accept, then, my eagerness, which goes beyond my ability, and grant us salvation: freedom from the passions of the soul, relief from the diseases of the body, release from hardships, a peaceful course of life, the illumination of the Spirit. Kindle our longing for your Son; make our life pleasing to him; so that we too, having attained the blessedness of that world and seeing you shining with the glory of your Son, may send up holy hymns, rejoicing for ever in the assembly of those who keep festival in a way worthy of the Spirit, to him who through you built our salvation, Christ, the Son of God and our God. To him be glory and power, with the Father who has no beginning and the all-holy and life-giving Spirit, now and always and to all the endless ages of ages. Amen.

choices.note: Luke 1:28 is printed in italics with Migne's margin ('Luc.
John 1:29 is a clear unmarked quotation (the Lamb of God who takes away the sin of the world). 1 Corinthians 1:24 cited for 'the power of God and the wisdom of God'.
χαῖρε / χαίροις rendered 'Rejoice', and Luke 1:28 given as 'Rejoice, you who are full of grace; the Lord is with you' to match Homilies I and II.
The whole litany (to 'servant and mother') is the hymn introduced by 'chanting something like this', so it stands inside one quotation.

Left uncited as possible only: Song of Songs 4:15 / Jeremiah 2:13 (spring of living water), Song of Songs 2:1-2 (rose, lily), Matthew 6:28-29 (lilies and royal clothing), Luke 1:38 (δούλη, handmaid), Romans 6:8 / 2 Timothy 2:11 (dying and living with), 1 Peter 2:24 (ἀπογινόμενοι, dying to).
Readings: printed πνέων (masculine) where the neuter πνέον would agree with ῥόδον; sense unchanged ('breathing out the fragrance').
ἄγαλμα rendered 'ornament' (LSJ: glory, delight, ornament, votive statue);
'image of the Holy Spirit' was avoided because it would suggest Mary images the Spirit, which the word need not mean.
ἐξόδιον λόγον rendered 'discourse on your departure', keeping the funeral/exodus sense used for ᾠδὴν ἐξόδιον in 3.3.
δεξαμένη taken as 'whom you served when ... you received'.
ἀκουτισθῶμεν ('let us be made to hear') rendered 'let us listen'.
'ἐν ἐκκλησίᾳ ἑορταζόντων ἀξίως τοῦ Πνεύματος' rendered 'in the assembly of those who keep festival in a way worthy of the Spirit' (Latin 'qui pro dignitate Spiritus festa celebrant').
The long final period is split into three English sentences; every clause is kept.
This is the end of Homily III;
Migne's next item (John of Damascus's encomium on John Chrysostom) is not part of this work.
